meta.title: Squad: manager–worker coordination
meta.subtitle: Local CLI calls share durable state—not an autonomous agent scheduler. Source pinned at 8146bcc.

components.label: Manager terminal
components.explanation: The manager is an external agent following role instructions, not a running controller inside Squad. It checks agents, creates tracked assignments, and receives replies. To see task completion it can run task list; complete_task itself does not send a result message. A worker can explicitly send a summary instead. Inspector review is a role convention outside this diagram's manager–worker scope.

components.label: Squad CLI
components.explanation: One squad invocation runs the requested command. It walks up to a .squad workspace and opens .squad/messages.db. join registers a unique active agent ID, writes a local session token and prints role instructions; it does not launch the worker or model. Actor commands check active identity/session and touch last_seen. receive --wait uses locks/<agent>.receive.lock, rechecks the captured session, polls every 500 ms and heartbeats every 30 s. Missing local session files are accepted for backward compatibility; this is not a remote authentication boundary.

components.label: Worker terminal
components.explanation: The worker executes the actual work outside Squad. For a structured assignment it receives the task-linked message, explicitly acknowledges the task, then explicitly completes it with a summary. Freeform coordination uses send/receive. Both terminals invoke the same CLI implementation against the same workspace; there is no direct manager-to-worker transport in this path.

components.label: Task commands + Store
components.explanation: create_task requires active creator and assignee and atomically inserts both a queued task and an unread task_assigned message carrying task_id. ack requires queued status and the assigned active agent; a conditional UPDATE sets acked and a 15-minute lease. complete requires acked status and that active lease owner; it writes the summary and timestamps but sends no message and does not test lease expiry. requeue is explicit, clears lease/results and can change the assignee; it creates no new assignment message. Without --to, the implementation sets assigned_to to NULL rather than preserving it. list reads persisted tasks.

components.label: Messaging + Store
components.explanation: send inserts an unread note, optionally with task_id and reply_to. Direct recipients must be active; @all fans out to active agents other than the sender. receive atomically selects unread messages and marks those IDs read, then CLI renders text or JSON. A task_assigned message is enriched by looking up its current task record. Reading a message does not acknowledge the task. Messages are retained as read history; the read transaction commits before terminal output, so this is not processing acknowledgement or a proven exactly-once delivery guarantee.

components.label: .squad/messages.db
components.explanation: A single local SQLite file is shared by independent CLI processes. Store owns SQL I/O, enables WAL and a 5-second busy timeout, and creates/migrates the tables. agents holds identity, role, status, client/protocol metadata, last_seen and session token. tasks holds assignment, status, lease, result and timestamps. messages holds sender/recipient, content, read flag, kind, task_id and reply_to. Client/protocol metadata is recorded, but the shown task creation path does not gate on protocol version or manager role.

connections.label: insert notes; read + mark inbox; task lookup

cards.title: Assignment is not acknowledgement
items: create → queued task + unread task_assigned message in one transaction.
receive → message read; task stays queued. ack → acked + 15-minute lease; only the active assignee can ack.
complete → completed + result_summary; only the active lease owner can complete. No automatic result message.

cards.title: How the manager gets the result
items: task list reads the persisted status and summary; worker send → manager receive is a separate, explicit notification path.
CLI arrows represent invocations; reads return through the CLI as stdout text or --json. Both actors must share the workspace.
Roles are printed guidance, not role-based authorization: create checks active agents, not a manager role or protocol capability.

cards.title: Local boundaries and limits
items: Session files: .squad/sessions/<id> (src/session.rs:5–22,50–59). Wait lock: locks/<id>.receive.lock, outside .squad (main.rs:796–814).
No automatic lease-expiry recovery in the traced path: complete does not check expiry. Explicit requeue clears state but emits no new message (store.rs:653–719).
